ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 makes the no-show fee conditional on the driver having done BOTH things before cancelling: sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call. The record satisfies only the call limb. The trip record's contact_before_cancel block reports message_count 0 against an empty messages array (source EV-CHAT-05053) while listing two calls (12:17:55 and 12:19:40). One limb of a conjunctive obligation is not the obligation, and POL-NS-23 states in terms that where either is missing 'the fee is voided and the rider is not charged'. The 5.00 SGD fee must therefore be voided.

The chat log independently confirms the omission rather than merely failing to record a message: it holds exactly one entry and that entry is the rider's own — 'Coming down now, sorry', sent at 12:21:50 and delivered at 12:21:53 — 40 seconds AFTER the driver cancelled at 12:21:10. Every driver-side entry in the log is absent, and none exists in the window between auto-arrival at 12:15:30 and cancellation at 12:21:10. There is no message to weigh in the driver's favour.

The driver's failure to message was not a matter of opportunity. The driver-device trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 — 24 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps, corroborating the 12:15:30 arrival — and its fixes report zero speed from 12:15:14 through 12:20:44, i.e. the vehicle was standing at the pickup for the whole waiting window. The driver found the time to place two calls in that window (12:17:55 and 12:19:40) but sent no message at any point. The gap POL-NS-23 exists to catch is squarely present.

Expiry of the free wait does not carry the fee on its own. POL-NS-21 governs the 300 s wait running from arrival (12:15:30 to 12:20:30), and the cancellation at 12:21:10 came after it; but expiry does no more than permit a driver to cancel, and POL-NS-22 charges the 5.00 SGD fee only for a cancellation that is a valid rider no-show. POL-NS-23 is a separate, independent precondition on that same cancellation, and the rider's position is that the free wait plus a non-compliant cancellation cannot combine into a chargeable no-show.

The driver's statement that he 'called two times, no answer', and the rider's own admission that his phone was on silent, go only to the call limb. POL-NS-23 places the obligation on the driver's acts — one message and one call — not on the rider's responsiveness: an unanswered call is precisely the situation in which the message limb does its work, by putting in writing where the driver is waiting. The rider's silence cannot supply the message the driver never sent, and the fee does not become chargeable because the rider was unreachable.

POL-NS-23 fixes the consequence of the breach: FULL_REFUND of the fee charged, with no driver compensation. The payments ledger shows 5.00 SGD charged at 2026-08-12T12:21:14 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the whole contested 5.00 SGD is still outstanding and money remains to be moved. Under POL-GEN-03 a FULL_REFUND is measured against the filing party, and the rider filed, so returning the full charge is the rider's win and driver_compensation_sgd is null.

No fact POL-NS-23 needs is missing, so there is nothing here for POL-GEN-26 to escalate. The call log and timestamps are carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, and the message count is carried by the COMPLETE chat log at weight 1.0. The one absent artifact, EV-ADVIS-05053-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; no clause in the no-show category requires a traffic advisory, so it carries no fact for either side and does not open a question. Neither does it assist the driver: an absent third-party record cannot stand in for the message POL-NS-23 requires.

The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and the two artifacts that carry the deciding fact are COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes fired. Nothing on this record raises the confidence bar or pushes the case to human review, so the AI ruling is final and can issue the FULL_REFUND now rather than holding the 5.00 SGD.

The driver's no-show cancellation was timely and its arrival is corroborated, so the precondition for a no-show under POL-NS-21 is met: the auto-arrival at 12:15:30 is supported by the GPS trace (nearest fix 3.07 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m arrival radius for this STANDARD-zone pickup, reported accuracy 6 m; 24 fixes at 30 s intervals and no gap over 30 s), and the cancellation at 12:21:10 falls 340 s after arrival, past the 300 s free wait.

The call limb of the driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is satisfied on the face of the record: the driver placed two in-app calls to the rider - at 12:17:55, ringing 20 s unanswered, and at 12:19:40, ringing 18 s unanswered - both before the 12:21:10 cancellation, and both carried in trip_record.in_app_calls and in the platform event log.

The substance of a rider no-show, which is what POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD fee exists to compensate, is established on this record: the GPS trace carries no rider track at all, the driver's fixes sit at 0 kph at the pickup from 12:15:14 through 12:20:44, and the rider's only message ('Coming down now, sorry') was sent at 12:21:50, 40 s after the driver had already cancelled.

Any remedy should not exceed the fee actually charged: POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is available only where the driver 'also failed to attempt contact', and the two unanswered in-app calls show contact was attempted, so no goodwill credit and no referral under that clause is warranted.

I concede the point that governs this reference: trip_record's contact summary records message_count 0 with an empty message list and obligation_met false, and the chat log - COMPLETE at weight 1.0, contiguous, its single entry matching trip_record.chat_message_count - holds only the rider's 12:21:50 message. No in-app chat message was sent by the driver before cancelling, so the message limb of POL-NS-23 fails, and on that clause's terms the fee is voided; I do not put a case that the fee stands.

Neither profile can ground a finding here: POL-GEN-01 permits only rider_profile.fraud_flags, driver_profile.fraud_flags and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d to be cited, the driver's fraud_flags is absent (0) and the rider's no_show_cancellations_30d is 0, so the driver's prior no-show history on his profile is context only and cannot be used to condemn his conduct on this trip.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged at 2026-08-12T12:21:14 is refunded in full to the rider.

Why, to the driver: your arrival and your waiting are not in doubt. The auto-arrival at 12:15:30 is corroborated by the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05053, COMPLETE, weight 1.0 — nearest fix 3.07 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD-zone arrival radius, reported accuracy 6 m), and your cancellation at 12:21:10 falls 340 s after arrival, past the 300 s free wait (POL-NS-21). You also made the calls: two in-app calls, at 12:17:55 and 12:19:40, both unanswered, both before cancellation (EV-TRIP-05053), and this is borne out by your own statement that you 'called two times'. But POL-NS-23 (v2.1 2.3) makes the fee conditional on the driver having done TWO things before cancelling for a no-show: sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call. One limb of a conjunctive obligation is not the obligation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05053, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) holds exactly one message, and it is the rider's — 'Coming down now, sorry', sent at 12:21:50, delivered 12:21:53, forty seconds after you had already cancelled. The trip record's own contact summary (EV-TRIP-05053) records message_count 0 with an empty message list and obligation_met false. No driver message exists anywhere in the window from 12:15:30 to 12:21:10. POL-NS-23 states in terms that if either limb is missing the fee is voided and the rider is not charged, so the fee does not stand and POL-NS-22 does not carry it to you as compensation.

To the rider: the amount returned is the whole 5.00 SGD contested. The payments ledger (EV-FARE-05053, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) shows 5.00 SGD charged and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so 5.00 SGD is outstanding and is now returned to you. The fee is exactly the policy figure (POL-NS-22), so no amount adjustment arises.

Points the driver raised, answered. (1) That the substance of a no-show is established — no rider track, your vehicle stationary at 0 kph through 12:20:44, the rider's message arriving after cancellation — is accepted as far as it goes, but it cannot rescue the charge: POL-NS-23's message requirement is a separate, independent precondition on the cancellation, not an element of the rider's absence. (2) That the calls satisfy the contact obligation is accepted, but only the call limb; POL-NS-23 requires both. (3) The rider's silent phone does not supply the missing message: the obligation is on the driver's own acts, and an unanswered call is precisely the situation in which a written message does its work. (4) No goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 is due: that credit requires that the driver also failed to attempt contact, and you did attempt contact twice (and, this being an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, there is no lateness deadline against which a driver no-show could be fixed).

Referrals. None arises. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check adds nothing because the amount charged is exactly 5.00 SGD. POL-NS-25 does not fire: the rider's profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d count, and the fee does not stand. POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire for the reason just given.

Confidence and who decides. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band; there are no fraud flags on either party; and no safety indicator appears. Under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final at any confidence. The facts deciding this case are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0 with no issue codes fired (EV-TRIP-05053, EV-CHAT-05053, EV-FARE-05053, EV-GPS-05053); the one absent artifact, EV-ADVIS-05053-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 and no no-show clause requires a traffic advisory, so it carries no fact and opens no question under POL-GEN-26. Ruling: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, with no driver compensation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
